title: Cap. X: Placeus — same will explains the discrimination without antecedent imputation
pass_a_gloss: First Placeus can scarcely stop marveling at the learned man's absurdity (ἀτοπίαν): he does not notice that Placeus's side can equally seek the reason of this discrimination from God's will. Nothing easier than to answer that every vice's contagion is such that it can spread and propagate like plague, poison, or leaven unless God's providence or grace sets a barrier. So the discrimination proceeds thus: God did not will to stop the first parent's vice from being propagated by carnal generation; but He did will to restrain other parents' other vices from multiplying the same way by natural propagation — so that in the one case the force of sin and nature, and in the others the force of God's providence and grace, could be seen.
pass_b_english: What first strikes me is the learned man's sheer absurdity: he never sees that we, no less than he, may fetch the reason of this discrimination from God's will. The easier reply is ready. Every vice carries a contagion able to spread like plague, poison, or leaven — unless providence or grace from God throws a barrier across its path. On that footing the discrimination is plain. God refused to block the first parent's vice from running on through carnal generation; yet He chose to check other parents' other vices so that natural propagation would not multiply them likewise. Thus in Adam what belongs to sin and nature stands out, and in the rest what belongs to God's providence and grace.
source_text: Primum satis mirari nequeo viri docti ἀτοπίαν, non animadvertentis, nos pariter a Dei voluntate hujus discriminis rationem petere posse. Quid enim facilius quam respondere, ejusmodi esse omnis vitii contagium, ut instar pestis, vel veneni, vel fermenti sese diffundere & propagare possit, nisi Dei vel providentia vel gratia obicem ponat. Discrimen igitur inde procedere, quod primi parentis vitium Deus, quominus per carnalem generationem propagaretur, noluit impedire: Aliorum vero parentum alia vitia, ne similiter propagatione naturali multiplicarentur, inhibere voluit; ut in illo quae peccati & naturae; in his quae Dei providentiae & gratiae vis esset, perspici posset.

choices.decision: Dei voluntas explains discrimination for propagation side too
providence/grace can block vice-contagion like plague
